Elena (CSM): Heads-up — MediAtlas sent back their vendor questionnaire and flagged a few onboarding blockers: they want BYOK, a dataflow + network diagram for SOC2 evidence, and explicit embeddings retention policy. Can we triage?
Ben (Security): On it. Can someone drop the PDF link so I can see exact BYOK wording and subprocessors ask?
Elena (CSM): Link: https://files.mediatlas.co/qa-2026.pdf — KMS questions on p3, data residency + logs on p7.
Jin (Legal): They also uploaded a redlined DPA requesting a list of subprocessors and a clause around key custody. We'll need to provide the subprocessors manifest and a short SOC2 scope blurb.
Ravi (Eng): I can sketch the dataflow diagram and env inventory (prod/dedicated, staging, non-prod). Do they want CIDRs or a logical flow?
Elena (CSM): They asked for both if available, but legal said a logical diagram plus endpoint list is usually enough.
Ben (Security): Quick KMS note we should include in the response: Redwood supports customer-managed keys in Private and Dedicated deployments; Hosted customers can use our managed KMS or opt into BYOK when on a Private plane. Key points to call out: provenance (customer-imported vs Redwood-provisioned), rotation controls, and whether HSM-backed attestation is required. Example snippet to paste into questionnaire:
```
kms:
  supported_modes: [managed, byok]
  byok_providers: [aws-kms, gcp-kms, azure-keyvault]
  byok_notes: "BYOK available for Private and Dedicated; hosted BYOK possible on case-by-case with contract + onboarding."
```
Ben (Security): Also: we should explicitly state that keys in Dedicated/Private are under customer control and that Redwood never persistently stores plaintext key material.
Marta (Product): Customer feedback: these vendor forms are painful. I'll create a "concise answers pack" template mapping our short canonical answers to typical questionnaire questions (KMS, subprocessors, logs, retention). We can attach that to future DPAs.
Elena (CSM): MediAtlas said the length is a blocker — this would help. If Marta can draft the pack, we'll include it with the DPA response.
Jin (Legal): For the DPA redline: we'll provide a subprocessors link and propose a rolling notice clause for new subprocessors. I'll prepare the legal language and sign-off.
Ravi (Eng): For embeddings: we store embeddings encrypted at rest with default TTL 90 days for short-lived projects; for production customers we support configurable retention policies and can set a customer-specified TTL at onboarding. I'll add that to the diagram and the concise pack. Also note: non-prod uses ephemeral keys and redaction on PII.
Elena (CSM): Action items — please confirm ETA next to each: 
- Ravi: dataflow diagram + env inventory + embeddings retention blurb (EOD tomorrow)
- Ben: BYOK explainer + raw-log access sentence (tomorrow)
- Marta: concise answers pack draft (48h)
- Jin: subprocessors manifest + DPA guidance (48h)
I'll tentatively schedule an enablement call with MediAtlas Tue 10am PST — hold that slot.
onboarding-bot: Ticket created: CS-4821 MediAtlas DPA intake — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-4821. Assignees: Elena, Ben, Ravi, Marta, Jin.
Elena (CSM): MediAtlas also asked for clarity on "access to raw logs". Suggested one-liner for pack: "Authorized ops and security personnel may access request logs for up to 30 days for debugging and security investigations; sensitive fields are redacted and access is logged/audited."
Ben (Security): That wording works. I'll add a note about audit trails and role-based access controls.
Marta (Product): I'll incorporate the sentence and create the concise pack sections: Required (regulatory/SOC2 items) vs Optional (implementation details). Opening a product ticket to propose the split; will share a draft by EOD Friday.
Jin (Legal): Once the pack + diagrams are ready, I'll review and return a single response package for Elena to send.
Elena (CSM): Thanks — I'll update MediAtlas and upload all artifacts to CS-4821 so the customer has a single source. Please post any attachments there.
